analysis.manifestationCriterion: per fault and rate, one cell: the frontend pause manifests if at least 90 % of the requests scheduled in the first 45 s of the hold fail and checkout requests sent in them (by send time) succeed in at most 10 % of cases (the pause command takes a moment to bite); an off-path pause manifests if the target service's consumer-side spans started in the hold number at most 10 % of those started in the pre-onset 60 s AND checkout requests scheduled in the hold keep succeeding (at least 95 % ok); in every case the rate's no-fault cell shows neither the effect nor the failure, and a valid no-fault cell that fails its precondition (checkout rows and all rows >= 95 % ok in its pseudo window) makes the verdict '—' for that rate

manifestationCriterionDefaults.frontendPause: ledger rows scheduled in [onset, onset + 45 s) (the hold minus the client timeout of 15 s: a request scheduled later can be served after the unpause inside its own timeout; request-ledger.json, every route): the share with outcome ok is <= 10 %, and the checkout rows (route=checkout) SENT in it (startedAtEpoch - barrierEpoch in [onset, onset + 45 s), because a checkout waits for its cart POST and can leave its slot by up to 20 s) succeed in <= 10 % (the first requests before the pause bites succeed); the no-fault cell's rows in the same window at its pseudo onset succeed in >= 95 % (each share needs >= 20 rows, else '—')
manifestationCriterionDefaults.minimumSpans: a segment with fewer than 20 spans of the statistic gives '—' for that statistic
manifestationCriterionDefaults.noFaultCell: the same statistics at its pseudo onset must show neither the effect nor the failure
manifestationCriterionDefaults.noFaultPrecondition: a valid no-fault cell must itself be healthy in its pseudo hold [onset, onset + 60 s): checkout rows (route=checkout, scheduled in it) >= 95 % ok and all rows >= 95 % ok, each with >= 20 rows; if it is not, the verdict of every fault at that rate is '—' (the fault's effect cannot be told from a baseline that already fails), not 'does not manifest'; this is a property of the cell, reported with the numbers
manifestationCriterionDefaults.offPathPause: consumer-side spans of the target service: service.name = the target (frauddetectionservice or accountingservice) and Kind=Consumer; count started in the hold <= 10 % of the count started in the pre-onset 60 s (pre-onset count >= 20, else '—'); AND checkout rows (route=checkout) scheduled in the hold: outcome ok >= 95 % (and >= 20 rows, else '—'); AND the no-fault cell at its pseudo onset has a hold/pre-onset count ratio > 10 % and its checkout rows >= 95 % ok
manifestationCriterionDefaults.onset: fault cells: intervention.json freeze.commandIssuedOffsetSeconds (= actualOnsetMonotonicOffsetSeconds, pre-command), mapped to wall clock with request-ledger.json barrierEpoch; no-fault cell: its pseudo onset, timing.scoredWindowSeconds[0]
manifestationCriterionDefaults.spanSelection: by span start time; all spans regardless of status; spans from otelcol.log (Start time, UTC)
manifestationCriterionDefaults.unit: one cell per (fault, rate); a verdict is per (fault, rate); a fault is kept for campaign F iff it manifests at >= 1 rate
manifestationCriterionDefaults.validCell: a cell counts iff its host receipt says valid and an offline validate_cell replay of it passes (the witness check runs only in the terminal); the no-fault cell of the rate must be valid too, else the verdict is '—'
manifestationCriterionDefaults.verdict: manifests / does not manifest / '—' (a statistic below its minimum, an invalid cell, an invalid no-fault cell, or a no-fault cell that fails its precondition, at that rate)

faultCells.rule: windows by request start on the fault receipt's monotonic clock. Fault cells: pre-onset = start before the onset command was issued; fault-and-drain = start in [onset command issued, route ready + drainSeconds]; after-drain = later. No-fault cells: one whole-measurement window. (i) incomplete traces of fault-and-drain requests are counted and recorded (with request tokens) as the fault's effect, never blocking; (ii) the cell is blocked only if the successful requests of the other windows with an incomplete trace number more than max(allowanceMinimum, floor(allowanceShare x their successful requests)). Complete = the request's own trace id observed and every service its route is guaranteed to reach (workload.mix.routes[route].requiredServices, a conservative subset) observed in that trace (a request of the mix has its route's set; services beyond the set, such as flagd or the async consumers, are neither required nor unexpected; C's 'exactly the route's services' was for its single route). Every incomplete trace is counted per window (successful and unsuccessful separately) in trace-completeness.json, evaluated on the target before the next cell and replayed by the terminal

noFaultCells.authority: research/PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md decision 56 (user 2026-10-04, round 12, on research/traffic-sweep/STOP_QUIET_OTEL_A1.md); this epoch only, the sweep keeps decision 25
noFaultCells.decision25Counterfactual: recorded per cell, not applied: max(allowanceMinimum, floor(allowanceShare x successful requests)) and whether the incomplete count exceeds it
noFaultCells.rule: one whole-measurement window (every cell is a no-fault cell). Complete = the request's own trace id observed and every service its route is guaranteed to reach (workload.mix.routes[route].requiredServices, a conservative subset) observed in that trace (a request of the mix has its route's set; services beyond the set, such as flagd or the async consumers, are neither required nor unexpected; C's 'exactly the route's services' was for its single route). A successful request without a complete trace is telemetry loss: counted and recorded, never blocking. trace-completeness.json records per window the successful, complete and incomplete requests (unsuccessful separately); for every incomplete request its scheduled offset, whether its own trace id was observed and which required path services were missing; the count of incomplete requests per missing service; and the contiguous runs of consecutively scheduled requests that are each successful and incomplete (first and last scheduled offset, request count, missing services), so a lost export batch shows as one run. Evaluated on the target before the next cell and replayed byte for byte by the terminal

freezeStamps.dockerEvents: pause cells only: docker-events.json, kind otel-demo-fault-docker-events-v1, retained beside intervention.json. A live `docker events` stream (filters type=container, event=pause, event=unpause, label com.docker.compose.project=<project>) is started before the measurement barrier and stopped after the fault worker has settled, so the daemon's bounded event buffer cannot lose the event. The file holds the stream's raw JSON lines, the parsed events (action, containerId, service, timeNano, monotonic and barrier-relative offset by the cell's mapping), parseProblems for lines that could not be parsed, and the mapping. Verdict {status ok|missing|contradictory, failures, reasons[{kind, reason}], ...}: ok iff the stream was alive when stopped, there is exactly one pause event and one unpause event of the target container, the pause event lies in [commandIssued, commandReturned] and the unpause event in [revertCommandIssued, revertCommandReturned], each widened by the declared tolerance (0.25 s), and the unpause follows the pause; absences are missing, anything that disagrees is contradictory
freezeStamps.onsetInterval: pause: [commandIssued, Docker pause event]; throttle: [commandIssued, commandReturned] plus the applied quota read back
freezeStamps.receipt: intervention.json freeze = {schemaVersion 1, kind otel-demo-fault-freeze-stamps-v1, action, commandIssuedMonotonic (= startedMonotonic), commandReturnedMonotonic (taken when the fault command returns, before the state readback), stateReadbackMonotonic (= appliedMonotonic), the three barrier-relative offsets, dockerEventsFile, stampCheck {status ok|missing|contradictory, failures, reasons}}; expected: commandIssued <= commandReturned <= stateReadback, issued = startedMonotonic, readback = appliedMonotonic, returned <= revertingMonotonic
freezeStamps.rule: H4 never invalidates a cell. A failed, dead or contradictory event stream or stamp leaves the cell valid and the freeze record marked missing (an absence: no stream, no event) or contradictory (events or stamps that disagree), with its reasons and a failure count per cell, in docker-events.json verdict and in intervention.json freeze.stampCheck. The terminal replays and byte-compares whatever was retained: a record that does not replay from its own raw lines, clock and receipt is refused (integrity), a record that replays and says missing or contradictory is accepted (availability)
freezeStamps.throttleStamps: command issued and command returned monotonic stamps and the applied-state readback stamp; no events

faultDesign.manifestation: pause: the paused container state read back after the command; throttle: the applied NanoCpus read back. The Docker pause event is evidence recorded beside it, not a condition of manifestation (decision 69). The entry route is not probed during the fault (scenario entryRouteDuringFault is not-probed-h10). Off-path pauses (frauddetectionservice, accountingservice) are proven by the paused container state read back and the Docker pause event, like the frontend's; whether the consumer-side effect shows in the target's spans, and that checkout requests keep succeeding, is the pilot's question, re-measured here per block (analysis.manifestationCriterion), not a harness condition

timing.duringFaultProbeRule: H10: no readiness probe from the fault onset to the end of the hold (scored window [onset, onset + hold]); the post-revert readiness probes start after the revert command returns, and the stack and route readiness before the warm-up are unchanged

workloadMix.draws: every parameter is an integer from sha256(namespace NUL 'mix' NUL taskIndex NUL label) mod n (no stdlib RNG): identical on 3.9 and 3.13, a pure function of (runId or warm-up namespace, task index)
workloadMix.journeys: a task is a journey: its requests are adjacent plan slots and run sequentially in the open loop's slots; a request that needs a predecessor's effect (POST /api/checkout needs the cart the preceding POST /api/cart filled, held in valkey under the journey's userId) is dispatched at max(its slot, the predecessor's end), is sent even if the predecessor failed (upstream's behaviour; no row is skipped, so every offered token is witnessed), and records its predecessor (dependsOn) in its row
workloadMix.propagation: every request carries traceparent 00-<trace id>-<span id>-01 and x-obsplacement-request-token, one trace per request, the offpath identity rule (candidate_remote.request_identity); the upstream loadgenerator is removed
workloadMix.requestOrder: the tasks' requests in task order, flattened; request i is scheduled at barrier + i / rate; the last task is cut at the cell's offered count
workloadMix.requestShares: per 24 tasks (34 requests with multiAdds' mean of 3): GET /api/products 16 (47 %), POST /api/cart 6 (17.6 %), recommendations, ads and view-cart 3 each (8.8 %), POST /api/checkout 2 (5.9 %), GET / 1 (2.9 %) (DESIGN.md 2.3)

add-to-cart.derivation: frontend pages/api/cart.ts POST -> cartservice AddItem, then GetCart (valkey); no productcatalogservice call

ads.derivation: frontend pages/api/data.ts -> adservice GetAds (-> flagd); a None category sends no query (requests drops None); upstream spells the path /api/data/ and relies on Next.js's 308 redirect to /api/data (trailingSlash is unset), which Python 3.9's urllib does not follow and which would show the request token to the proxy twice, so the canonical path is sent (a declared deviation in spelling, not in route)

checkout.derivation: frontend pages/api/checkout.ts -> checkoutservice PlaceOrder -> cartservice GetCart/EmptyCart, productcatalogservice GetProduct, currencyservice Convert, shippingservice GetQuote (-> quoteservice) and ShipOrder, paymentservice Charge, emailservice (HTTP), then the order message to Kafka topic orders (asynchronous: accountingservice, frauddetectionservice, whose consumer spans start their own traces, so they are never in the checkout request's trace); the offpath epoch's path check observed these ten plus flagd on every successful journey

index.derivation: frontendproxy -> frontend renders the shell; the product list is fetched client side (pages/index.tsx)

product.derivation: frontend pages/api/products/[productId]/index.ts -> productcatalogservice GetProduct; flagd only for OLJCESPC7Z (productcatalogservice main.go checkProductFailure); no currency call without a currencyCode

recommendations.derivation: frontend pages/api/recommendations.ts -> recommendationservice ListRecommendations (-> flagd, productcatalogservice ListProducts), then productcatalogservice GetProduct for up to 4 products

view-cart.derivation: frontend pages/api/cart.ts GET -> cartservice GetCart (valkey); upstream sends no sessionId, so the cart is the empty one of session '' and no productcatalogservice call follows

workloadMix.sessions: userId = 'u' + first 24 hex of sha256(namespace NUL 'mix' NUL taskIndex NUL 'user'), one per journey, so carts never mix across journeys (upstream uses uuid1 per journey); GET /api/cart sends no sessionId, as upstream

source.dropped: flood_home (weight 5: issues get_flagd_value('loadgeneratorFloodHomepage') homepage requests, 0 at the default flag, and asks flagd on every call); the 1-10 s think time (arrival spacing replaces it); the browser (Playwright) tasks; the baggage and OTel instrumentation of the Locust process; on_start's index request

workloadMix.taskOrder: smooth weighted round-robin (nginx's algorithm) over the integer task weights, ties to the earlier task; 24 tasks per cycle, so every window of one cycle holds each task's weight exactly

workload.arrivals: constant spacing (offset = sequence / rate) from the shared barrier, over the requests of the mix; the rate is the total requests per second of the whole mix
workload.concurrencyRule: ceil(2 x rate x request timeout) = ceil(2 x 25 x 15) = 750: the worker cap covers rate x timeout with the sweep's 2x margin; one thread per in-flight, waiting or scheduled-ahead request
workload.generatorOpenFiles: the controller raises its RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit to concurrency + 1024 = 1774 (never above the hard limit) before the cell starts, or refuses the cell: every in-flight request holds a socket, and an EMFILE would read as a failed request of the target
workload.ledger: request-ledger.json (kind otel-demo-mix-ledger-v1): one row per scheduled request with its route, task, journey, step, method, target, bodySha256 and dependsOn, scheduledOffsetSeconds, scheduledAtEpoch, startedAtEpoch/endedAtEpoch, startedMonotonic/endedMonotonic (the fault receipt's clock), status, bytes, error and outcome ok|timeout|failed; the terminal replays every row's identity, route and parameters from the plan

upstreamGenerators.mechanism: docker compose rm --stop --force loadgenerator, after up and before readiness
upstreamGenerators.proof: upstream-generator.json per cell: zero containers carrying the project's service label after the removal and after the window (asked of the Docker engine)
upstreamGenerators.why: the upstream Locust loadgenerator runs in every offpath/v3 cell (LOCUST_HEADLESS true overrides LOCUST_AUTOSTART false; retained v3a2 b03-03-full otelcol.log: 360 loadgenerator records, Starting Locust 2.18.2, GET http://frontend-proxy:18080/ failing) and asks flagd on every task; the sweep's rate must be the only traffic

workload.warmup: 30 s at 10/s of the same mix (its own token namespace), never scored
workload.window: the workload returns no earlier than barrier + measurementSeconds at every rate (the CPU and capture windows are the same length at every rate)
